title: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (main)
quote: Allocate speculative lookahead slots later to avoid mismatching local and remote block counts. / We don't schedule partial draft tokens since this prevents uniform decode optimizations. / Prefer to not schedule than schedule un-padded.
proves: vLLM V1 calls allocate_slots(request, num_new_tokens, num_lookahead_tokens=self.num_lookahead_tokens) inside schedule(), before the forward pass, for every running request; waiting requests get the same lookahead unless they have an async KV load. num_new_tokens comes from num_tokens_with_spec, so draft tokens consume token_budget; drafts are scheduled all-or-nothing and new decode requests are padded to 1+num_spec_tokens to keep full CUDA graphs. On allocation failure the scheduler preempts running[-1] (or lowest priority) and frees all its blocks; a step that preempts admits no waiting requests.
does_not_prove: Does not show how many blocks the lookahead actually adds per request (at most one block per request when K < block_size) or how often lookahead causes a preemption that a non-spec run would not have. No measurement.
bearing: Supports any idea about lazy/elastic lookahead reservation or spec-aware admission; shows the reservation is static per step and preemption is all-or-nothing.

title: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py (main)
quote: num_lookahead_tokens: The number of speculative tokens to allocate. This is used by spec decode proposers with kv-cache such as eagle.
proves: allocate_slots sizes the request to min(num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, max_model_len) and allocates blocks for new + lookahead tokens; only verified tokens are cached (capped at request.num_tokens). No code in allocate_slots frees lookahead blocks after rejection; rejected-token rollback is mentioned only for skipped-block freeing.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify waste; lookahead blocks are reused next step by the same request, so the cost is a transient per-request block, not a leak.
bearing: Bounds the size of the reservation waste (sub-block per request); threatens ideas that assume large lookahead waste in vLLM chain drafting.

title: [Performance]: Dynamic speculative decoding (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse under concurrency at the batch-size threshold (MTP, V1/PIECEWISE) (vLLM issue 49548)
quote: Reserved lookahead slots are normally transient, but they still count against the free-block admission check
proves: With dynamic K, num_lookahead_tokens stays fixed at the static num_spec_tokens, so lookahead is reserved even when the per-batch K is 0. Reporter saw 8 concurrent x 180 tokens drop from ~232 tok/s aggregate to 24-157 tok/s (Qwen3.5-122B MTP k=2, GB10).
does_not_prove: The lookahead hypothesis is the author's lowest-confidence one and was never tested; follow-up PR 51466 found no throughput gain and was closed. Collapse is more likely CUDA-graph dispatch related. Open, no maintainer reply.
bearing: Open question: whether reservation should track the dynamic K. Weak support for a reservation-sizing idea; strong warning that the collapse cause is unconfirmed.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix speculative block reservations across KV cache groups (vLLM PR 59880)
quote: under-reserving these blocks can leave a request admitted for an asynchronous KV load but unable to start decoding
proves: vLLM already reserves spec-decode blocks at admission for async KV loads (reserved_blocks); before this fix (merged 2026-10-11) the reservation was under-counted for multi-group / hybrid models. Fix sums reservation per cache manager by block size; in-flight lookahead accounting moved into cache managers; Mamba excluded from admission margin.
does_not_prove: Correctness fix with tests only; no capacity or throughput numbers. Reviewer estimate of ~1 block per Mamba group over-reserve is not measured.
bearing: Shows spec-aware admission reservation exists in vLLM now; threatens 'nobody accounts for speculative reservations at admission'.

title: [P/D][Bugfix] Fix PD async KV load lookahead handling for MTP spec decode (vLLM PR 46694)
quote: Fix NIXL async KV load handling for speculative decoding by deferring lookahead slot allocation during remote KV receive.
proves: Merged 2026-07-09: lookahead slots are deferred while a request receives remote KV in P/D, because eager lookahead made local and remote block counts disagree.
does_not_prove: Deferral is limited to the P/D receive step, not a general lazy-reservation policy; no memory numbers.
bearing: Shows deferral of lookahead is already practiced in one path; partial threat to a 'deferred lookahead' idea, support for generalizing it.

title: [Bug]: [PD + SpecDec] Prefix-cache trimming drops wrong block when P has extra lookahead block (vLLM issue 43996)
quote: P keeps its full num_lookahead_tokens, so at block boundaries P allocates one more block than D.
proves: Lookahead reservation on the prefill node (which never decodes) creates an extra block at block boundaries and a wrong-block transfer bug.
does_not_prove: Closed as not planned (stale); correctness only, no capacity cost measured.
bearing: Evidence that lookahead reservation is applied where it is useless (prefill role); supports role-aware reservation ideas.

title: [Bugfix][Core][Spec Decode] Skip spec-decode block reservation on the external-KV-load step (P/D) (vLLM PR 50173)
quote: the decode over-allocates KV blocks on a request's initial external-KV-load step
proves: Both the lookahead reservation and pad_spec_decode over-allocate on the first decode step after KV transfer: DeepSeek-R1 TP8 1P1D MTP1 block_size=64, 959-token prompt: P sent 15 blocks, D reserved 16, crashing on assert; fix gives 512/512 gsm8k completions.
does_not_prove: Open, not merged, needs rebase. Harm is a crash, not capacity; one surplus block per request.
bearing: Shows reservation semantics still being patched case by case (Jul-Oct 2026); weak support for a principled reservation model.

title: [Core] Avoid mixed batch on spec-dec D-node via padding (vLLM PR 45237)
quote: This PR lets the decode-side scheduler optionally pad the first post-transfer step with dummy speculative tokens
proves: Padding a newly transferred request to 1+N dummy spec tokens keeps the batch on the full CUDA graph. GLM-5.1 NVFP4 8xB300: mean TPOT 38.83 ms padding off vs 16.99 ms on; CUDA graph launches 44 to 1. Padding is coordinated across DP ranks.
does_not_prove: Single-run numbers; the dummy-token padding also costs KV slots and compute that the PR does not measure.
bearing: Shows deliberate over-reservation (padding) is a net win for latency; threatens ideas that treat padding as pure waste.

title: [RFC]: Automate Speculative Decoding (vLLM issue 4565)
quote: For instance, if num_lookahead_slots is set to 5 but the proposed length is only 3, then 2 slots would go unused.
proves: The vLLM spec-decode authors named the static lookahead-slot reservation vs dynamic proposal length as a memory inefficiency in 2024.
does_not_prove: Closed as not planned (stale, 2025); V0-era; no measurement of the waste.
bearing: Shows the over-reservation gap was known and never quantified or fixed; supports a measurement-first candidate.

title: [RFC]: Sparse-attention-based self-speculative decoding (StreamingLLM, then Vegas) (vLLM issue 47351)
quote: Reserves lookahead slots so KV pages are allocated for draft tokens
proves: New proposers (self-speculation) plan to reuse the same lookahead-slot reservation mechanism.
does_not_prove: No memory analysis; RFC is stale.
bearing: Weak: shows lookahead reservation is the default design for new proposers.

title: Spec v2 tree drafting (topk>1) with page_size>1 (SGLang PR 26972)
quote: the draft reserves a page-aligned per-branch footprint of `2 * get_alloc_len_per_decode`
proves: SGLang tree drafting with topk>1 and page_size>1 reserves 2 x (topk x num_new_pages x page_size) slots per request per decode; before the fix (merged 2026-06-06) over-allocated slots were never freed (pool leak) and indexing overflowed. Row widened to max(4 + num_draft_tokens, 2*alloc_len).
does_not_prove: No numbers on how much KV the page-aligned tree reservation costs at batch scale.
bearing: Strong support: tree speculation with paging multiplies reservation by topk x page_size; a measurable over-reservation gap.

title: [Bug] Prefill out of memory during eagle_worker verify (SGLang issue 13765)
quote: compute an appropriate KV cache buffer size for the speculative decoding process of each request
proves: SGLang EAGLE verify failed allocating 508 tokens with 448 available when the pool was full; reporter proposed a per-request reserved speculative KV buffer accounted for by the scheduler. Others reported similar retractions.
does_not_prove: No maintainer reply; auto-closed as inactive; reporter's diagnosis unconfirmed.
bearing: Supports 'spec KV is not reserved at admission in SGLang, so verify can OOM at high load'.

title: [Bug][Speculative] EAGLE/MTP causes 90% KV cache starvation on models with untied embeddings (Fix Included) (SGLang issue 44145)
quote: this locks out over 90% of the KV cache capacity permanently
proves: Single GPU: KV pool 225,211 tokens without spec, 15,363 with stock EAGLE MTP, 169,603 with patch (draft embedding/LM head counted before sharing). Opened 2026-10-13, fix PR 45151 open.
does_not_prove: A memory-profiling bug for one model class, not an inherent cost of speculation; even patched, capacity drops 25%.
bearing: Strong evidence spec decode can silently cost large batch capacity; supports measurement of capacity cost per method.

title: Speculative Decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: These three parameters directly control how much memory the draft tree consumes
proves: SGLang docs: steps, topk and num_draft_tokens set draft-tree memory; spec decode may increase memory via draft tree, CUDA graphs and verification buffers; OOM advice is lower mem-fraction-static, cuda-graph-max-bs, tree size, or limit concurrency. Overlap scheduler supports only topk 1.
does_not_prove: No numbers; guidance is manual static tuning.
bearing: Supports 'reservation for speculation is set by hand, not by load'; candidate for automatic sizing.

title: tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/resource_manager.py (main)
quote: Dynamic-tree draft manager reserves K*max_draft_len KV slots (the draft loop can write that many even if max_total_draft_tokens is smaller).
proves: TRT-LLM admission budget per request is blocks to completion for prompt + max_new_tokens + num_extra_kv_tokens + _kv_reserve_draft_tokens; each generation step adds 1 + max(draft_len, reserve) tokens, then rewinds rejected tokens (rewind_kv_cache). Dynamic-tree drafter reserves topK x max_draft_len slots.
does_not_prove: Source read only; no measurement of capacity lost. Fetched via curl, not WebFetch.
bearing: Shows a production engine reserves worst-case draft KV at admission (strict, mode-2-like); supports comparing strict vs optimistic reservation.

title: speculative decoding (vllm-metal docs)
quote: Its committed KV and speculative lookahead share the Metal KV memory budget with the target.
proves: On vllm-metal (user's hardware), draft_model uses a second scheduler-managed KV cache; MTP reads target KV; n-gram has no extra KV. The scheduler allocates both, no separate draft scratch pool. Experimental DFlash and DSpark use scheduler-owned cache lifecycle.
does_not_prove: Gives no sizes; the 'un-budgeted KV cache' phrase in an earlier search snippet was not on the page.
bearing: Makes a reservation experiment feasible on the M5: lookahead and draft KV come out of one budget the scheduler controls.

title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (blog)
quote: Inside the captured CUDA graphs cost is a staircase rather than a line, because of cudagraph padding
proves: A 121-token batch pays for the 128-token graph; budget B is chosen to maximize expected tokens per step time using load; slots compete across requests. Larger capture size needs more cudagraph memory, so the repro uses --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 because it OOMs at default.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about KV slots for drafted vs verified tokens; memory cost of graphs not quantified.
bearing: Shows verification compute is already allocated across requests by load (threat to verify-budget ideas); hints CUDA-graph memory is a hidden reservation cost.

title: Resource-Efficient Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Serving (SpecStream)
quote: GPU memory limits force additional requests to queue, causing AR and SGLang SD throughput to saturate.
proves: SpecStream keeps the full draft KV on GPU, which takes a growing share of memory with concurrency; offloads committed history to CPU (starts at 8 concurrent on Qwen3); keeps unverified candidates on GPU so rejections need no cross-device cleanup; 1.41x/1.32x over TriForce.
does_not_prove: Long-context, offloading setting; does not isolate the cost of speculative reservation vs draft KV history.
bearing: Shows draft KV share under concurrency is a recognized cost; commit-aware tiering is taken.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: Under high request load, the memory occupied by these draft models directly competes with the KV cache.
proves: Nightjar disables SD under load and offloads the draft model to CPU when free KV blocks stay below a threshold; reload needs an empty queue and free blocks. SD degrades throughput up to 30.25% vs no-SD at high load; Nightjar up to 14.76% over standard SD.
does_not_prove: Reclaims draft weights, not lookahead/draft-KV reservations; 7B/13B scale.
bearing: Threatens 'reclaim speculative memory under pressure' ideas: draft-weight reclaim is done.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
quote: We find that the memory overhead of speculative decoding (SD) is minimal.
proves: Per-token KV: Llama3-70B 320 KiB target-only vs 352 KiB with 1B draft; Qwen3-8B 144 to 256 KiB with 0.6B draft. Reasoning workloads can trigger preemption once KV fills, so experiments were kept to medium batch.
does_not_prove: Does not measure maximum batch size or preemption rate with vs without SD.
bearing: Negative result for memory-cost ideas: authors call overhead minimal, but the Qwen3-8B 78% per-token increase and untested max batch leave the capacity question open.

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
quote: bounds the draft's KV working set to a constant
proves: Unread draft KV is 7.7-11% of total KV at 1M context; sliding window + sink on draft attention drops ~99% of draft KV entries, reclaimed via a ring buffer.
does_not_prove: Million-token regime; single author; abstract only.
bearing: Threat: shrinking draft-KV footprint is being done for MTP.

title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache
quote: add per-request memory and KV-write overhead that grow with concurrency
proves: Block drafters (DFlash-style) keep a separate drafter-side KV cache whose memory grows with concurrency; H-Spec removes it and reports lower KV utilization across concurrency levels.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no absolute memory or concurrency numbers.
bearing: Threat: drafter-KV elimination is recent and active (Sep 2026).

title: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Llama at Scale: Challenges and Solutions
quote: we add additional tree padding when allocating blocks for drafting and validation stages
proves: Meta production EAGLE: paged KV is not compatible with tree attention, so paging applies to the prefix only; separate base and draft caches; extra tree padding is reserved per block allocation so speculative tokens never cross block boundaries.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify the padding's memory cost or its effect on batch capacity.
bearing: Supports: production systems over-reserve for tree speculation; cost unmeasured.

title: SpecMemo: Speculative Decoding is in Your Pocket
quote: Speculative decoding pre-allocates a KV cache to use it as a scratch space and frequently update during verification stage.
proves: Memory model for Medusa trees: buffers scale with batch, tree nodes, candidates, levels, vocab; mask assumes full acceptance; pruning gives 65% runtime memory reduction keeping 96% throughput (Titan RTX 24 GB).
does_not_prove: Single-device, Medusa only; not a paged serving engine.
bearing: Threat to tree-buffer-shrinking ideas on small devices.

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
quote: necessitates a host-side post-processing step after each verification
proves: Saguaro's engine preempts sequences when lookahead reservations cannot be satisfied and deallocates pages beyond the accepted suffix after each verification; speculation cache is around hundreds of MB.
does_not_prove: No measurement of reservation-induced preemptions or host-side cost.
bearing: Shows reserve-then-reclaim with preemption is the standard pattern; cost of that pattern unmeasured.

title: Striking the Right Balance between Compute and Copy: Improving LLM Inferencing Under Speculative Decoding (BMC)
quote: This extra space can be repurposed for speculative decoding.
proves: BMC preallocates KV rows in chunks and uses the padding rows for speculative tokens (wasted rows 7 to 3 in an example); 1.23x geomean over vLLM. Notes vLLM allocates every 16 or 32 tokens.
does_not_prove: CPU-focused, OPT models; no high-load capacity measurement.
bearing: Partial threat: 'reuse padding for draft KV' is taken.

title: AdaServe: SLO-Customized LLM Serving with Fine-Grained Speculative Decoding
quote: The total number of nodes across all token trees must not exceed the hardware budget.
proves: Per-request minimum accepted tokens derived from TPOT SLO; per-step verification budget from hardware profiling split across requests' trees.
does_not_prove: Budget is compute per step; no KV memory accounting for trees.
bearing: Threat to SLO/latency-reservation-for-verification ideas: done for compute.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
quote: reformulates speculative execution as a budgeted scheduling problem
proves: High-concurrency regimes make verification compute dominant; static trees cause massive verification waste; ECHO in SGLang shifts budget between depth and width.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; compute budget, not memory reservation.
bearing: Threat to verify-budget ideas at high load.

title: TreeSpark: Calibrated, Load-Adaptive Draft Trees for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
quote: gracefully shrinks the tree back to the chain
proves: Load-adaptive tree size: under rising load the tree shrinks to a chain; 15-25% more accepted tokens per round than a tuned chain.
does_not_prove: Does not discuss KV memory or reservation for tree nodes.
bearing: Threat: load-adaptive tree width (and hence its reservation) is covered for compute.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: near-zero waste in KV cache memory
proves: Baseline: on-demand block allocation replaced max-length reservation, reducing KV waste from fragmentation and duplication and allowing larger batches.
does_not_prove: Predates spec-decode lookahead; does not cover per-step speculative reservation.
bearing: Known baseline: any reservation idea must beat on-demand + preemption.

title: Overcommit Accounting (Linux kernel docs)
quote: Heuristic overcommit handling. Obvious overcommits of address space are refused.
proves: OS baseline has three modes: heuristic (default), always overcommit, never overcommit (strict commit limit, allocations fail early instead of later kills).
does_not_prove: Analogy only. Maps to TRT-LLM (strict worst-case draft reserve, B15) vs vLLM (per-step optimistic lookahead with preemption, B1).
bearing: Frames a candidate: compare strict vs optimistic speculative reservation policies.

title: TransKV preprint on transactional speculative KV under paged memory (TechRxiv)
proves: Search snippet only: keeps speculative KV in a token-sized side buffer and commits accepted prefix to paged cache; up to 1.78x concurrency on P100/T4.
does_not_prove: Fetch failed (HTTP 403 via WebFetch and curl). Title, numbers and claims unverified.
bearing: If true, direct threat to a 'side buffer for speculative KV' idea; must be read before proposing one.

title: MineDraft: A Framework for Batch Parallel Speculative Decoding
quote: the performance of standard SD is often limited by the strictly sequential execution
proves: Two-batch overlap of drafting and verification as a vLLM plugin; up to 75% throughput gain.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention KV allocation; the search-snippet claim that it defers vLLM KV block allocation for drafted-but-unverified requests was not verified (PDF fetch exceeded size limit).
bearing: Possible threat to deferred-allocation ideas; verify full text.

title: Behind the Stack, Ep 13: Faster Inference: Speculative Decoding for Batched Workloads
quote: In high throughput workloads, the limiter is often KV cache capacity, not compute.
proves: Practitioner framing: when batch is KV-capacity bound, SD amortizes KV movement over more accepted tokens.
does_not_prove: Illustrative numbers only; does not quantify SD's own KV cost.
bearing: Supports that spec reservations matter exactly in the KV-bound regime where SD is pitched.
